$comment: Schedule task permission policy (Testing #79042): the expected allow / deny answer of every actor and operation, as rules over actor attributes and two settings. The Java helper matrix (SchedulePermissionHelperMatrixTest) and the e2e entry-point matrix (stylebi-enterprise e2e/tests/api/schedule/permission-matrix) both read this file. Rules are proposed until the test lead confirms them. An expression uses the attributes, the settings share (schedule.options.shareTaskInGroup) and deleteOnlyByOwner (schedule.options.deleteTaskOnlyByOwner), other rule ids, true / false, and && || ! ( ). Every refused request must answer an error and change nothing.

attributes.orgAdmin: organization administrator of the task's org
attributes.shareMember: in a group with the owner
attributes.grantHolder: explicit SCHEDULE_TASK READ+WRITE+DELETE on the task

rules.expr: siteAdmin || sameOrg && (orgAdmin || owner || ownerAdmin || grantHolder || share && shareMember)

rules.basis: ScheduleTaskService.canDeleteTask, with the explicit grant added

rules.changes: the public API run / get accept only explicit grants (no share group); EM run / stop and public stop skip SCHEDULER
EM / Portal editors ignore explicit grants; public API PUT / DELETE need only the grant and ignore deleteTaskOnlyByOwner; delete must check dependents at every entry point

rules.basis: internal-task targets (#77531), foreign owners on import, folder grants a site admin always has
import may name another user of the org as owner or execute-as only for an admin of that user
checkSaveRefusals: the owner (who runs the task) may not read the sheet / query / target, so even a site admin's save is refused
